front: What is Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) in one sentence?
back: RISC ISA dominating mobile and cloud — load/store architecture, fixed-width instructions, power-efficient — ARMv8-A / AArch64 ops debugging.

front: Explain the mental model of Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) (how the system thinks).
back: ARM (Advanced RISC Machine) uses Reduced Instruction Set Computing: simple instructions, register-register ops, explicit load/store to memory. AArch64 (64-bit) is the modern server and mobile baseline.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Advanced RISC Machine (ARM)?
back: Program Counter (PC) → fetch instruction → decode → execute → writeback → ARM pipeline: PC may read as current + offset (+8 bytes in AArch64 EL0 debug) → uname -m # aarch64 vs x86_64 → lscpu | egrep 'Architecture|Model name|Flags' → cat /proc/cpuinfo | head

front: Given a broken Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Program Counter (PC) → fetch instruction → decode → execute → writeback

front: What are the production-safe defaults for Advanced RISC Machine (ARM)?
back: Choose m7g / c7g instance families — verify binary has arm64 build Same app, ~20–40% better price-performance for many workloads vs x86

front: Symptom: Exec format error — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Wrong arch binary · Fix: Rebuild arm64 or use qemu-user

front: Symptom: Illegal instruction — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CPU feature mismatch · Fix: Check -march; avoid AVX-only code paths

front: Symptom: Slower than expected on Graviton — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: x86 emulation / wrong JDK · Fix: Native arm64 JDK/Node binary

front: Symptom: Docker pull wrong arch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Single-platform image · Fix: Manifest list with buildx

front: Symptom: Native module fail (node-gyp) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Prebuilt binary x86 only · Fix: Compile on arm64 CI

front: Gotcha with Advanced RISC Machine (ARM): what silently fails?
back: Assuming SIMD parity with x86 — NEON ≠ AVX512; vectorize carefully in crypto/video code.

front: When should you NOT use Advanced RISC Machine (ARM)?
back: Don't pick ARM for workload depending on proprietary x86-only libs without port plan. Desktop gaming GPU stack — still x86-heavy; ARM choice is workload-specific.

front: What is DSL (Domain Specific Language) in one sentence?
back: Language tuned to one problem domain — expressive for experts, useless elsewhere — contrast with general-purpose languages.

front: Explain the mental model of DSL (Domain Specific Language) (how the system thinks).

front: What is H3 (Hexagonal Hierarchical Spatial Index)?
back: H3 is an open-source spatial indexing system developed by Uber, designed to partition Earth into a uniform hexagonal grid hierarchy, enabling fast geospatial analytics and location-based data aggregation [h3geo.org+13Uber+13Uber+13](https://www.uber.com/en-BG/blog/h3/?ut…

front: What is Equidistant neighbors?
back: All six neighbors of any hexagon are equidistant—simplifying spatial computations and reducing directional bias common in square/triangular grids giskernel.com+2h3geo.org+2docs.heavy.ai+2.

front: What is Consistent area?
back: Hexagons offer more uniform coverage and lower quantization error for geographic sampling, compared to latitude-longitude grids Esri+9Uber+9Uber+9.

front: What is Ride-sharing & logistics?
back: Uber uses H3 to bucket live events (rides, driver positions) per cell to compute supply-demand patterns, surge zones, and dispatch decisions Uber+1Uber+1.

front: What is Spatial analysis & binning?
back: Easily aggregate large datasets by hexagon to visualize density, trends, hotspots, or to perform clustering across time and space Medium+1t1nak.github.io+1.

front: What is GIS & map rendering?
back: Integration with Elasticsearch, ArcGIS, React-Mapbox to visualize hexagonal heatmaps, boundary queries, or area-of-interest aggregation (e.g. walkability, network coverage) Reddit.

front: What is Big data & real-time?
back: Lightweight indexes, highly cacheable, efficient bitwise operations make H3 ideal for streaming or GPU-based pipelines Uber.

front: What is Approximate containment?
back: Child indices fit within parents approximately, not geometrically perfect—leading to small boundary discrepancies across resolutions h3geo.org.

front: What is Pentagonal anomalies?
back: Due to geometric constraints, 12 pentagons exist to compensate grid tiling—these may slightly distort adjacency in marine or pole regions Ubergiskernel.com.

front: What is Idempotent-key?
back: Idempotent request key validation prevents duplicate resource creation when a client retries a request (due to timeout, network failure, or duplicate submission) by using a unique key to detect and reject/duplicate repeat attempts.

front: What is Multi-tier and Layered Architecture in one sentence?
back: Tiers = where code runs (physical/deployment). Layers = how code is organized (logical/modules). A 3-tier web app can still be a spaghetti monolith inside the middle tier — Martin, Cockburn, Microsoft App Arch Guide.

front: Explain the mental model of Multi-tier and Layered Architecture (how the system thinks).
back: Multi-level architecture is two orthogonal axes:

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Multi-tier and Layered Architecture?
back: All concerns — UI, business logic, data — run in one process on one machine. → Client owns presentation + application logic; server owns data (database or file server). → Splits the 3-tier model for scale, security, or team boundaries: → Layers exist inside a monolith, microservice, or mobile app. Two common models — do not conflate them. → Martin organizes by policy stability, not call order. Inner = most abstract; outer = mechanisms/details.

front: Given a broken Multi-tier and Layered Architecture setup, what is your first validation command?
back: All concerns — UI, business logic, data — run in one process on one machine.

front: Symptom: "Works in Postman, wrong in UI" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Client doing business logic (2-tier leak) · Fix: Move rules to Service Layer; UI displays only

front: Symptom: Schema change breaks mobile app — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Fat client queries DB or embeds SQL · Fix: API versioning; server-owned contract

front: Symptom: Random data corruption — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Handler writes DB without transaction · Fix: Wrap multi-table updates in service txn (ACID)

front: Symptom: Can't unit test without Docker — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Domain imports ORM/HTTP types · Fix: Introduce ports (Martin DIP); in-memory adapters for tests

front: Symptom: ORM models used as domain entities — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: @Entity annotations in "domain" package · Fix: Separate entity from persistence model; map at adapter boundary

front: Symptom: DB row / ResultSet passed to use case — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Framework data structure crossed inward · Fix: Map to simple DTO in repository adapter before returning

front: Symptom: Folder layout says "Spring" not "Billing" — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Framework-screaming structure · Fix: Reorganize by use case (Screaming Architecture — see below)

front: Symptom: 15-hop sync chain, cascading timeouts — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: N-tier / microservice sprawl · Fix: Merge services or go async; backpressure

front: Symptom: "Distributed monolith" — must deploy all 12 together — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Shared DB, shared libs, circular calls · Fix: Database-per-service; define bounded contexts

front: Symptom: Layer violation in PRs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Controller imports repository directly · Fix: Enforce module boundaries (archunit, eslint boundaries)

front: Gotcha with Multi-tier and Layered Architecture: what silently fails?
back: Tiers ≠ layers. A team that "went to microservices" but kept one shared database and synchronous chains still has a distributed monolith — worst of both worlds.

front: When should you NOT use Multi-tier and Layered Architecture?
back: Rule of thumb: Default to 3-tier deployment + layered (or hexagonal) monolith. Split tiers and services when you have measured pain: deploy frequency, scale shape, blast radius, or compliance boundary — not because the diagram looks enterprise.

front: What is Orchestration layer in one sentence?
back: Workflow orchestration vs choreography — where Temporal, Airflow, Camunda, and step functions sit — distributed systems design.

front: Explain the mental model of Orchestration layer (how the system thinks).
back: Orchestration: a central coordinator drives steps, knows global state, retries, timeouts, compensations. Choreography: each service reacts to events with no central brain — flow emerges from message contracts.

front: Symptom: Stuck workflow — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Temporal UI / Airflow task logs · Fix: Retry policy; unblock signal; kill zombie run

front: Symptom: Double charge / ship — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Idempotency keys missing · Fix: Idempotent-key on activities; dedupe table

front: Symptom: Lost saga state — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Choreography-only — no central view · Fix: Add correlation ID logging; consider orchestrator

front: Symptom: Airflow backlog — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Scheduler health; pool slots · Fix: Scale workers; reduce concurrency cap

front: Symptom: Version skew — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Worker deploy mid-workflow · Fix: Temporal workflow versioning; compatible activity changes

front: Symptom: "Works in dev" timeout — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Step Functions 25s lambda limit · Fix: Break steps; use activity workers

front: Gotcha with Orchestration layer: what silently fails?
back: Orchestrator as SPOF — HA cluster + persistence (Temporal/Camunda DB) required for prod.

front: When should you NOT use Orchestration layer?
back: Single CRUD service — domain logic in app code suffices. Sync request/response chain < 3 hops — direct calls + Idempotent-key. Replace kafka with Airflow — different problems; often complement (Airflow consumes Kafka).

front: Design a minimal correct Orchestration layer setup for a small production service.
back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: Workflow orchestration vs choreography — where Temporal, Airflow, Camunda, and step functions sit — distributed systems design.

front: What is QUIC in one sentence?
back: UDP-based transport with built-in TLS 1.3, multiplexing, and faster handshakes — HTTP/3 foundation.

front: Explain the mental model of QUIC (how the system thinks).
back: QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connections) moves transport into user space over UDP, integrating encryption and stream multiplexing. Designed to fix TCP head-of-line blocking and slow connection setup for web apps.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for QUIC?
back: HTTP/3 → QUIC (streams, crypto, congestion) → UDP datagrams → IP → curl -I --http3 https://cloudflare.com

front: What are the production-safe defaults for QUIC?
back: Browsers upgrade from HTTP/2 via Alt-Svc: h3=":443" — first visit may still use h2.

front: Symptom: Never see h3 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: UDP 443 blocked · Fix: Open firewall; CDN QUIC toggle

front: Symptom: Falls back to HTTP/2 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Alt-Svc missing/expired · Fix: Add Alt-Svc header; cert valid

front: Symptom: 0-RTT replay concerns — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Idempotent GET only · Fix: Disable 0-RTT for non-idempotent routes

front: Symptom: CPU high on edge — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: QUIC in userspace · Fix: Hardware TLS; tune worker count

front: Symptom: Connection migration fails — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: NAT rebinding · Fix: QUIC connection IDs — usually CDN handles

front: Gotcha with QUIC: what silently fails?
back: Middleboxes that block UDP — corporate networks may force HTTP/2 fallback; always serve h2/h1 too.

front: When should you NOT use QUIC?
back: Internal east-west microservice mesh on trusted LAN — gRPC over HTTP/2 may be simpler ops. Legacy clients only — maintain dual stack until analytics show negligible h3 need.

front: Design a minimal correct QUIC setup for a small production service.
back: Checklist: (1) mental-model constraint, (2) required config/commands, (3) health/triage check, (4) one failure mode to avoid. Anchor: HTTP/3
